description: One high-importance parent with children vs. an unrelated low-importance parent whose children look marginally more urgent on their own features. At the current 0.93/0.07 weighting, the children's own importance is close enough that the parent goal's importance still decides the order -- see notes.

notes: Written for an earlier 0.5*own + 0.5*mean(ancestors) weighting, where the parent goal's importance was strong enough to flip the across-group order despite task_low_1/2's higher own importance (0.7-0.8 vs 0.2-0.3). Revised down to 0.93*own + 0.07*mean(ancestors) (review on #474) broke that: 0.07 was too small for the 0.75-point ancestor-importance gap to outweigh a 0.5-point own-importance gap, so own importance alone already produced the (unchanged) expected order -- the fixture no longer demonstrated that propagation changes the outcome. Fixed by narrowing the own-importance gap instead of the ancestor gap: task_high_1/2 at 0.30/0.29, task_low_1/2 at 0.33/0.32 (max own-importance gap now 0.03, scaled by 0.93 = 0.0279) versus the unchanged 0.75-point ancestor gap (scaled by 0.07 = 0.0525) -- the ancestor gap now wins. Scores: task_high_1=0.93*0.30+0.07*0.9=0.342, task_high_2=0.93*0.29+0.07*0.9=0.3297, task_low_1=0.93*0.33+0.07*0.15=0.3174, task_low_2=0.93*0.32+0.07*0.15=0.3081 -- the high group now outranks the low group despite the low group's own importance being nominally higher, which a formula reading only the leaf's own score (or ignoring ancestors) would get backwards.
